Producer review feedback on CG-0MS934XSL00453HF (raised selection feature, currently in_review): when a card raises, the selection highlight does not raise with it. Additionally the raise slider should go to a maximum of 180px with a default of 60px.

Root cause: in HandView.updateSelectionTints(), applySelectionRaise(true) runs BEFORE the tint loop, so on first selection the raise tween starts before the tint overlay exists — the overlay is created at the resting position and is not in the tween targets, so the card raises while the highlight stays behind. Hover pointerover/pointerout also destroy+recreate the overlay, which can orphan it mid-tween.

## Acceptance criteria

1. Regression tests written FIRST (TDD): animated-path first-selection overlay is included in the raise tween targets; hover repaint reuses the overlay in place; reduced-motion first-selection overlay ends at the raised position.
2. The selection highlight overlay always ends at the raised position on first selection (animated and reduced-motion).
3. GymHandPileScene raise slider: RAISE_MAX = 180, RAISE_DEFAULT = 60; reset() restores the default; Controls help text updated.
4. HandView setSelectionLift() API default remains 0 (opt-in) — backward compatible.
5. npm run build succeeds and all HandView + Gym unit tests pass.
data.title: Gym Hand & Pile: selection highlight raises with the card; raise slider max 180 / default 60

## Summary

Research spike to determine the client-side follow-detection mechanism for the "Follow us on Steam" incentive. The Steam client SDK has no direct "user follows this game's store page" call, so candidates must be verified before committing. This feature produces the decision-gate report that F4 depends on.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A report documents and evaluates each candidate: `ISteamFriends::IsFollowing(<developer account>)` (client-side, no backend), Steam Web API `IPlayerService` (game-page follow, needs server + publisher API key), and any other client-side candidates discovered.
- [ ] The report states a recommendation and flags the UX impact of each candidate (e.g. follows developer account vs game page).
- [ ] The recommendation is confirmed with the user (decision gate) and recorded in this item before F4 implementation commits to a mechanism.
- [ ] Any unknown (e.g. whether a server component is acceptable) is surfaced as an open question with options, not silently assumed.

## Minimal Implementation

- Prototype a minimal probe using the Steamworks SDK against a real Steam account (dev environment with Steam running).
- Research Steamworks SDK docs / community reports for `ISteamFriends::IsFollowing` semantics.
- Write findings to the work item as a structured report (markdown), including a decision recommendation.
- No production code committed in this feature.

## Prototype/Experiment

Success = a clear recommendation with evidence (docs/community/experiment) that the implementer can act on without re-research.

## Dependencies

- Parent blocked-by CG-0MSMAD19O0084CAW (Electron launcher) — launcher must exist to run Steamworks in-app.

## Deliverables

- Decision-gate report (in work item comments).
- Confirmed mechanism choice.

Monte Carlo harness exposes BankingGreedyStrategy as a first-class, selectable strategy variant without replacing the existing greedy baseline.

- MonteCarloStrategy union extended with 'banking-greedy'; ALL_STRATEGIES includes it.
- createAiPlayerForStrategy('banking-greedy', seed, difficulty?) returns new MainStreetAiPlayer(new BankingGreedyStrategy(difficulty), rng); existing 'greedy' path still returns pure GreedyStrategy (verified by win-rate / action-type divergence test or strategy-name assertion).

# Intake Brief — Don't add coins/reputation/score until the end of the end of turn cycle (CG-0MTR72P14000VO6Q)

## Problem Statement

During the Main Street end-of-turn cycle, coins, reputation, and score are applied to `state.resourceBank` and `state.finalScore` **immediately** inside `processEndOfTurn()` (via `applyIncome()`, `resolveIncident()`, and `updateScore()`). The HUD display (`refreshHud()`) then reads these already-updated values and shows them instantly, while the end-of-turn animations (income collection, incident reveal) play afterwards. This creates a visual disconnect: the HUD shows new resource values before the coins fly from the card to the HUD display, and the game-over check (`checkEndConditions`) evaluates against the already-updated state before the player has seen the income feedback.

## Users

- **Main Street player** — wants resource changes to be visually synced: coins fly from cards to the HUD, *then* the HUD updates to reflect the new values. No premature game-over banners.
- **Main Street AI/headless sim players** — unaffected; the engine logic remains the same, only the presentation layer is affected.

### User Stories

- As a player, when I press "End Turn", I see the income coins animate from my producing business cards to the HUD display, and only after the animation completes do the coin/reputation numbers on the HUD update — so the visual feedback matches the state change.
- As a player, I should not see a game-over banner triggered by income that I haven't yet visually confirmed — the win/loss evaluation should happen after the final income animation lands.
- As a player, during the end-of-turn incident reveal, the coin/rep deltas from the incident should not appear on the HUD until the incident card's animation completes.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — Deferred state mutation:** `applyIncome()`, `resolveIncident()`, and any ongoing-cost deductions in `processEndOfTurn()` must **not** directly mutate `state.resourceBank` or `state.finalScore`. Instead, they compute deltas and return them in `TurnResult` as `pendingCoinDelta`, `pendingRepDelta`, and `pendingScoreDelta` (new fields).
- **AC2 — HUD persists pre-animation values:** During the end-of-turn animation window (`incomeCollectionActive` is true or an incident reveal animation is in flight), `refreshHud()` must display the **pre-animation** resource values (stored as `previousCoins` / `previousReputation`), not the mutated state values. The HUD only updates after the animation completes.
- **AC3 — State applied at animation end:** After the income collection animation (or incident reveal, whichever is last) completes, the pending deltas are applied to `state.resourceBank` and `state.finalScore` in a single step, followed by a final `refreshHud()` call. The `syncResourceBankToLedger()` is called after this final application.
- **AC4 — Game-over check deferred:** `checkEndConditions()` in `runSinglePlayerTurnClosing()` must NOT evaluate against post-animation state while animations are in flight. It should either: (a) run after the animation completes (recommended — restructure the closing flow so EndCheck runs after animation, or (b) accept the pending deltas as an optional parameter for the check.
- **AC5 — Reduced-motion mode:** When `reducedMotion` is true, there are no animations, so state is applied immediately as before (no regression). The deferred-path is only active when animations exist.
- **AC6 — Headless/AI sims unaffected:** `endTurnHeadless()` and the Monte Carlo harness continue to work without change — they bypass the presentation layer entirely. Engine logic (state mutations) still produces the same deterministic results; only the timing of HUD updates changes for the interactive path.
- **AC7 — All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.**
- **AC8 — Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.**

## Constraints

- The engine module (`MainStreetEngine.ts`) must remain deterministic and side-effect-free with respect to the HUD — engine mutations are for the AI/sim path only; presentation mutations happen in the scene/animator layer.
- `TurnResult` must carry all computed deltas so the scene layer can decide when to apply them.
- The `previousCoins` / `previousReputation` pattern (already used by `animateHudValueChanges`) should be extended to cover the end-of-turn window.
- No changes to game logic, economy calculations, or end conditions — purely a presentation/timing change.

## Existing State

- **`MainStreetEngine.processEndOfTurn()`** calls `applyIncome(state)` which mutates `state.resourceBank.coins` and `state.resourceBank.reputation` directly (MainStreetAdjacency.ts:683, 707).
- **`MainStreetEngine.processEndOfTurn()`** calls `resolveIncident(state)` which also mutates `state.resourceBank` (MainStreetEngine.ts:~1720).
- **`MainStreetEngine.runSinglePlayerTurnClosing()`** calls `updateScore(state)` which updates `state.finalScore` via `computeScore()` (MainStreetEngine.ts:1823).
- **`MainStreetRenderer.refreshHud()`** reads `s.state.resourceBank.coins` / `reputation` directly (MainStreetRenderer.ts:~398-400).
- **`MainStreetTurnController.endTurn()`** calls `processEndOfTurn()` then `finishTurnPresentation(result)` which calls `refreshAll()` / `refreshAllExceptStreet()` immediately after.
- **`MainStreetAnimator.animateHudValueChanges()`** already tracks `s.previousCoins` / `s.previousReputation` and suppresses HUD delta pops when `incomeCollectionActive` is true, but the HUD text values themselves are already updated by `refreshHud()`.
- **`checkEndConditions()`** runs during `runSinglePlayerTurnClosing()` (before the next day starts) against the already-mutated state (MainStreetEngine.ts:1830).

## Key Files (predicted)

- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetEngine.ts` — `processEndOfTurn()`, `applyIncome()`, `resolveIncident()`, `runSinglePlayerTurnClosing()`, `TurnResult` type — defer mutations, surface deltas
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetAdjacency.ts` — `applyIncome()` — compute deltas without mutating `state.resourceBank`
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetState.ts` — `resourceBank`, `finalScore` — may need pending delta fields
- `example-games/main-street/scenes/MainStreetTurnController.ts` — `endTurn()`, `finishTurnPresentation()` — apply pending deltas after animations
- `example-games/main-street/scenes/MainStreetRenderer.ts` — `refreshHud()` — display pre-animation values during animation window
- `example-games/main-street/scenes/MainStreetAnimator.ts` — `animateHudValueChanges()`, `animateIncomePhases()`, `animateIncomeCollection()`, `animateIncidentReveal()` — apply deltas on animation complete
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetScene.ts` — `previousCoins` / `previousReputation` tracking, `incomeCollectionActive` — extend to cover incident reveal too
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetEngine.ts` — `checkEndConditions()` — defer or pass pending deltas
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetCommands.ts` — may need updates if commands mutate resources

## Related Work

- **CG-0MTV69NII000LW8I** — "Position end-turn coin matrix on left side of card, growing right" (open, medium) — sibling presentation fix for the same end-of-turn income animation; the coin-grid anchor change is independent but should be merged close in time.
- **CG-0MSRGTUSK003GDGE** — "Animate end-of-turn income collection (coin fly-to-HUD)" (completed) — established the income collection animation that this task needs to respect.
- **CG-0MTW18KFK000MM3I** — "Incident reveal animation" (completed) — incident card flight + hold animation that also needs to respect deferred state.
- **CG-0MT5W7UJJ0065MEZ** — "In main street log should show total effects" (completed) — the per-turn net summary row; unaffected by this change.
- **CG-0MT23O6W8003AXWJ** — "Phased income show (base → synergy → rep → events → upcoming → grid-to-HUD)" (completed) — the phased choreography that this task must gate state updates on.

## Risks & Assumptions

- **Scope creep — re-architecting the engine:** The fix is presentation-layer only. Do NOT refactor `applyIncome`/`resolveIncident` to be purely functional (return-only) as that would break the headless sim contract. Engine mutations remain; the deferred-path applies them after animations.
- **Animation-completion callbacks:** Need a reliable mechanism to know when all end-of-turn animations have finished (income collection + incident reveal). The `incomeCollectionActive` flag plus a similar flag for incident reveal, or a single "closing animation active" flag with a completion callback chain, is the simplest approach.
- **Game-over timing edge case:** If the player reaches the score threshold during income, the game-over banner should only appear after the income animation completes, not before. This means `checkEndConditions()` may need to run after animation completes, which changes the current flow (currently runs before `startDayPhase()`). This is the correct behavior but needs careful restructure.
- **Undo/redo paths:** Undoing an end-of-turn action (if that were supported) would need to revert the pending deltas — but undo is cleared at end-of-turn anyway, so this is not a concern.
- **Assumption:** The engine (`MainStreetEngine.ts`) should still mutate `state.resourceBank` for the headless/AI path. The deferred mutation only applies to the interactive scene path. This keeps the engine module unchanged for non-interactive callers.

## Open Questions

- **Q1:** Should `checkEndConditions()` run (a) after animations complete and state is applied, or (b) immediately as it does now but using the pending deltas as a "what-if" evaluation? **Recommendation: (a)** — the game-over check should evaluate the final post-animation state, so the banner appears at the right visual moment. This means reordering `runSinglePlayerTurnClosing()` to defer EndCheck until after the animation window.
- **Q2:** The incident reveal animation (CG-0MTW18KFK000MM3I) also has resource deltas (`incidentCoinChange`, `incidentRepChange`) that mutate state. Should these also be deferred until after the incident reveal completes? **Recommendation: yes** — for consistency, all resource changes from the end-of-turn cycle should be deferred.
data.title: Don't add coins/reputation/score until the end of the end of turn cycle

# Problem statement

`implement.py finish` runs the pre-commit test gate with a hardcoded 600-second (10-minute) timeout via `run_cached(command, cwd=cwd, timeout=600, ...)`. TCE's full test suite (`npm test`) takes ~17–19 minutes, exceeding this cap. The timeout triggers `subprocess.TimeoutExpired`, the safety reset flips the work item from `in_progress` back to `open`, and every `implement.py finish` fails on first attempt.

# Users

- **AI agents** using the `implement` skill to complete tasks. They hit a silent timeout on `implement.py finish`, lose their `in_progress` status, and must manually pre-warm the test cache (a ~19-minute workaround).
- **Operators** reviewing work items that mysteriously flipped from `in_progress` to `open` after a timeout.

# Acceptance Criteria

1. **Config-driven timeout:** `implement.py` reads the per-command timeout from `.pi/test-config.json`'s `timeoutPerCommand` field with 600s as the default fallback when the file or field is absent.
2. **All `run_cached` calls use the resolved timeout:** Every call site that runs pre-commit/finish tests passes the resolved timeout (not a literal `600`) to `run_cached`.
3. **No regression on other repos:** Repos without `.pi/test-config.json` continue to use 600s as the default.
4. **TCE full suite passes:** On TCE, `implement.py finish` completes successfully without manual cache warm-up (timeout ≥ 1140s to cover the measured ~19 min with headroom).
5. **Documentation:** The `implement` skill's documentation or comment block documents how to override the test timeout via `.pi/test-config.json`.

# Constraints

- The fix is in a shared agent framework script at `~/.pi/agent/skills/implement/scripts/implement.py` (outside the TCE repo). Changes must be made in the agent-framework repository, not TCE.
- TCE's `.pi/test-config.json` already exists with `{"timeoutPerCommand": 1500}` — it was created for the test skill; this fix makes it also apply to the implement skill's gate.
- The change must remain backward-compatible with repos that lack `.pi/test-config.json`.
- The 600s default must be preserved as the fallback.

# Existing state

- `implement.py` lines ~1532, 1608, 1633, 1646, 1673, 1710 all hardcode `timeout=600` in `run_cached` calls.
- `run_cached()` (line ~1486) accepts a `timeout` parameter and passes it to `run_cmd()`.
- The test skill already reads `timeoutPerCommand` from `.pi/test-config.json` via `suite_timeout_per_command()` in `~/.pi/agent/skills/test/scripts/run_tests.py`.
- TCE's `.pi/test-config.json`: `{"timeoutPerCommand": 1500}`.

# Desired change

1. Add a helper function (or reuse the test skill's existing logic) in `implement.py` to resolve the per-command timeout: read `.pi/test-config.json` from the project root, extract `timeoutPerCommand`, fall back to 600.
2. Replace all hardcoded `timeout=600` in `run_cached` calls within the finish workflow with calls to this helper.
3. Document the override mechanism in the `implement` skill documentation.

# Key Files

- `~/.pi/agent/skills/implement/scripts/implement.py` — Add timeout-resolution helper; update `run_cached` calls
- `~/.pi/agent/skills/implement/SKILL.md` — Document `.pi/test-config.json` timeout override
- `/home/rgardler/projects/Tableau-Card-Engine/.pi/test-config.json` — Already present; no change needed (TCE side)

# Related work

- CG-0MT40CNO1002MSDC — Workaround: pre-populate test cache via test skill (manual ~19 min warm-up)

# Risks & assumptions

- **Risk:** `implement.py` may run in environments where the project root (for `.pi/test-config.json`) is ambiguous. **Mitigation:** resolve from `cwd` (the project root passed to the finish workflow).
- **Risk:** Adding a file-read dependency could fail on permission-denied or malformed JSON. **Mitigation:** wrap in try/except; fall back to 600s default; log a warning to stderr.
- **Assumption:** `.pi/test-config.json` follows the same schema as the test skill's config (flat JSON with `timeoutPerCommand` as an integer).
- **Scope creep:** Consideration of making other timeouts (git operations, builds) also config-driven is out of scope; this item only addresses the pre-commit test gate timeout.

# Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: Where is the fix applied — in the TCE repo or the agent-framework repo? — Answer: Agent-framework repo (`~/.pi/agent/skills/implement/scripts/implement.py`). Evidence: the script lives outside the TCE repo.
- Q: What is the correct timeout for TCE? — Answer: `.pi/test-config.json` already has `timeoutPerCommand: 1500` (25 min), which covers the ~19 min measured duration.
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **CG-0MSAZL6O2008PTWY** – [test-failure] Replay CLI tests in tests/replay/replay.test.ts (spawnSync node --import tsx/esm scripts/replay.ts exceeds 15s) — failing test (completed)
- **CG-0MPD5XSKC009UCTJ** – Gym Graphics: Scene Transitions & Camera Effects (Router + GymSceneBase) (completed)
- **CG-0MQK03TE4005FP3A** – More intuitive chopsticks UX (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `docs/DEVELOPER.md` — matched: absent, acceptance, accepts, add, adding (+165 more)
- `AGENTS.md` — matched: acceptance, add, adding, agent, agents (+139 more)
- `docs/main-street/prd-balance-process-and-tooling.md` — matched: absent, add, adding, agent, agents (+106 more)

# Staff underlay rendering and tooltips

## Summary
Render a graphical staff-count underlay (count badge) on business slots that display employed staff, plus a tooltip that enumerates each employed staff member and their effects.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Staff count badge**: A small graphical overlay on each business slot showing the number of employed staff (e.g. a rounded badge in the corner of the slot, or a subtle count underlay beneath the card).
2. **Tooltip enumeration**: Hovering a business slot with employed staff shows a tooltip that lists each employed staff member's name, their allowedBusinessTypes, and their active effects (income bonus, reputation bonus, special abilities).
3. **Tooltips aggregated**: Tooltip aggregates the business's own info (income, reputation, synergy) with the employed staff's buffs.
4. **No overlay conflicts**: The staff underlay does not break existing upgrade overlays (level badge, income display), synergy animations, or sold-state visuals (SOLD overlay).
5. **Empty state**: Slots with no employed staff show no badge and tooltip shows only business info.

## Minimal Implementation

- In `drawBusinessSlot()` in MainStreetRenderer.ts, after applying upgrade overlays, add a count badge rectangle/text if business.employedStaff.length > 0
- Badge positioned at bottom-right corner of slot (SLL-defined anchor)
- Extend tooltip zone to show staff enumeration when employed staff exist
- Reuse existing tooltip rendering infrastructure (buildCardTooltipInfo or similar) with staff enumeration data

## Deliverables

- `example-games/main-street/scenes/MainStreetRenderer.ts` -- staff count badge + tooltip enumeration
- Browser test: staff underlay + tooltip rendering
- Visual confirmation: badge visible at all zoom levels, tooltip readable

## Key Files

- `example-games/main-street/scenes/MainStreetRenderer.ts`
- `tests/main-street/staff-underlay-rendering.browser.test.ts` (new)

## Dependencies

- Depends on: CG-0MU3BNO590066H75 -- Staff business-type matching engine

Add a section to the implement skill documentation explaining how agents/operators can override the default 600s test timeout by creating .pi/test-config.json with a timeoutPerCommand value at the project root. Reference the test skill's existing documentation of this pattern.

data.description:
## Goal

Write unit tests that verify per-action challenge evaluation works correctly before implementation begins.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Tests verify that evaluateChallenges() returns IDs of newly completed challenges when called after an action that satisfies a challenge condition.
2. Tests verify that calling evaluateChallenges() a second time on the same state returns an empty array (already-completed challenges are idempotent).
3. Tests verify the end-of-turn safety net path: when challenges were already completed mid-action, the end-of-turn call must not double-report (return empty for already-completed challenges).
4. Tests cover at least 3 challenge types: resource (Deep Pockets), placement (Bustling Street), and synergy (Foodie Row).

## Key Files

- tests/main-street/challenges.test.ts — new test file for per-action evaluation
- example-games/main-street/MainStreetChallenges.ts — evaluateChallenges function under test
- src/core-engine/ChallengeSystem.ts — generic evaluateChallenges that Main Street wraps

## Dependencies

None — this is the first task.
